Scale journey from surface to eye to veins to a cellular ripple suggests choreographed match-cuts
The body-interior metaphor (blood, eye, veins) is a well-worn thriller/medical titles trope, so the idea is solid but expected
gaps: The idea is the familiar 'inside the body' title sequence; tie the imagery to a narrative motif specific to the show, as the best Art of the Title entries do
Typography is tasteful but conventional (a thin sans dropped into negative space); let the credits interact with the fluid and tissue as C's best frames integrate elements
Monochrome red risks monotony across a full sequence; introduce one controlled counter-tone or shift in light to give it an arc

defects: Line-up board hold is about 3.4 s of rows filling one by one into a static grid. It reads as a slideshow, not choreography, and the empty Q6–Q8 rows look unfinished as a frame.
Name cards (DVS1, KIA) only get a small scale punch or nudge between frames, so it is the same move every time, with no anticipation, overshoot or settle.
The lightning shows up only in the opening and the dates shot and is dropped in the line-up and ticket shots, so the strongest device is never followed through.
The FRIDAY grey ghost is caught half-faded in a sampled frame, which looks like an opacity crossfade rather than a designed transition.
The bolt is a generic procedural arc with little branching variety, and its glow pops between frames instead of flickering with any build or decay.
Audio is a sine-sweep kick repeated on a fixed grid, plus a white-noise riser and a hard cut. There are few partials and no mid-range musical content, so it reads as generated.
The pure black name cards drop the grain and glow used in the other shots, so the texture is inconsistent between scenes.
gaps: Motion has no physical language. The bolt should drive everything: names struck or energised in, rows charging along a circuit, a discharge as the release. Instead it is cuts and scale bumps on a beat grid, with no spacing curves, overlap or weight.

No arc or payoff. Energy starts at maximum, sags through the long line-up hold, and the riser at 9.4–13.1 s resolves into a plain ticket card. A world-class version would peak around 70% and end on a bolt that rhymes with the SUB/STATION opening.

Sound design is thin and static: one repeated synthetic kick and a noise sweep. It needs a produced techno bed, electrical crackle and hum tied to the bolt, sub impacts on the cuts, and real dynamic contrast.
